places.hours_text: Open 7 days, 9.30 a.m. to 8.15 p.m. dine-in, 8.30 p.m. drive-through — the 6th Avenue room
places.name: Big Bob Gibson Bar-B-Q
places.blurb: The Decatur, Alabama pit where white barbecue sauce was invented: mayonnaise, vinegar and black pepper, made for smoked chicken.

places.name: Wing It On Wings and Wiches

places.hours_text: Monday to Thursday 11 a.m. to 2.30 a.m.; Friday and Saturday 11 a.m. to 3.30 a.m.; Sunday noon to 10 p.m.
places.name: Yum's II Carry-Out
places.blurb: A Chinese carryout on 14th Street NW in Washington, open past two most nights, selling fried wings, fried rice and french fries with mumbo sauce over them. It is the first address on most D.C. carryout lists.

places.name: Hooters
places.blurb: A restaurant chain that sells breaded wings, beer and a uniform. Six Clearwater, Florida businessmen incorporated Hooters, Inc.

places.name: American Deli
places.blurb: A counter chain out of Atlanta, open since 1989, that sells wings by the ten-piece with a long board of seasonings and sauces.

places.name: Buffalo Wild Wings
places.blurb: A sports-bar chain that put a Buffalo wing on a menu in Columbus, Ohio in 1982 and then on menus in all fifty states.

places.name: J.R. Crickets
places.blurb: A Midtown Atlanta wing bar open since 1982, founded by Paul Juliano, who still runs it.

places.hours_text: Open daily from 11 a.m. to midnight, as reported in June 2025
places.name: The Wing Cafe & Tap House
places.blurb: A wing bar on Roswell Road in east Cobb County, outside Atlanta, carrying thirty-five to forty sauces and marinades and thirty to fifty beers on tap.

places.name: Harold's Chicken Shack
places.blurb: A Chicago fried-chicken institution founded by Harold Pierce in 1950 and franchised to friends and family, now past a hundred storefronts.

places.name: Uncle Remus Saucy Fried Chicken
places.blurb: A West Side Chicago fried-chicken counter whose sauce is in its name. Gus W. Rickette Sr. and Mary F.

places.name: Capital City Mambo Sauce
places.blurb: A bottler, not a counter. Arsha and Charles Jones started Capital City in a home kitchen in 2011 to put D.C.

places.name: Horace & Dickie's Seafood
places.blurb: A fried-fish carryout that ran thirty years at 12th and H Streets NE in Washington and now trades from Prince George's County, Maryland.

places.name: Anchor Bar
places.blurb: A bar and restaurant at Main and North in Buffalo, open since 1935, which claims the Buffalo wing and has trademarked the phrase. Frank and Teressa Bellissimo opened it; their son Dominic ran it and sold the story.

places.name: Atomic Wings
places.blurb: A New York wing chain founded in 1989 by a man trying to reproduce what he had eaten as a student in Buffalo.

places.name: Bar-Bill Tavern
places.blurb: A tavern on Main Street in East Aurora, fifteen miles southeast of Buffalo and not in the city at all, whose wings are brushed with sauce by hand rather than tossed.

places.hours_text: Open daily; closing runs late and varies by night and by the sports calendar
places.name: Blondies Sports
places.blurb: A sports bar on West 79th Street between Amsterdam and Broadway, on Manhattan's Upper West Side, with televisions in every sightline and a wing order most of the room is there for.

places.hours_text: Monday to Thursday 11am–9pm, Friday and Saturday 11am–10pm, Sunday noon–9pm
places.name: Country Sweet Chicken & Ribs
places.blurb: A Rochester counter open since 1977, hand-breading its wings and glazing them in a sauce the founder built in a home kitchen and the city now buys by the bottle.

places.hours_text: Sunday to Thursday 11am–9pm, Friday and Saturday 11am–10pm
places.name: Duff's Famous Wings
places.blurb: A wing house at Sheridan Drive and Millersport Highway in Amherst, north of Buffalo, open under that corner since 1946 and selling wings since 1969.

places.hours_text: Monday 11:30am–2am; Tuesday 11:30am–11:30pm; Wednesday to Friday 11:30am–2am; Saturday noon–2am; closed Sunday
places.name: Elmo's Bar & Restaurant
places.blurb: A pitcher-and-television sports bar on Millersport Highway in Getzville, near the University at Buffalo's north campus, whose signature is a wing that goes through the fryer and then onto a grill.

places.hours_text: Monday to Thursday and Sunday 11:30am–midnight; Friday and Saturday 11:30am–1am
places.name: Gabriel's Gate
places.blurb: A restaurant and tavern at 145 Allen Street in Buffalo's Allentown, trading since 1969 inside an 1864 brick row house with tin ceilings and two wood-burning fireplaces.

places.hours_text: Monroe Avenue: Sunday to Wednesday 11am–11pm (kitchen to 10pm); Thursday to Saturday 11am–midnight (kitchen to 11pm)
places.name: Jeremiah's Tavern
places.blurb: A tavern at 1104 Monroe Avenue in Rochester, the first of four rooms, frying wings that arrive "fresh, never frozen" in sauces the company mixes daily at its own commissary.

places.name: La Nova Pizzeria
places.blurb: A pizzeria on West Ferry Street in Buffalo's west side, run by three generations of the Todaro family, whose barbecue wing is the local counter-argument to cayenne and butter.

places.name: Mammoser's Tavern & Restaurant
places.blurb: A neighbourhood tavern on South Buffalo Street in Hamburg, twelve miles south of the city, pouring eighteen microbrew drafts and frying a wing in a house sauce built on four kinds of pepper.

places.hours_text: Kitchen Tuesday to Thursday 4:30–9pm, Friday and Saturday 4:30–9:30pm; bar until 10pm and 10:30pm
places.name: Nine-Eleven Tavern
places.blurb: A cash-only corner tavern in South Buffalo, established 1981, whose wings come out large and heavily sauced in a recipe its late owner kept to himself.

places.hours_text: The Flatbush Avenue counter runs to 6am; no source read here gives its days. The Prospect Place room posts 11am daily, closing between 10pm and 12:30am.
places.name: Peppa's Jerk Chicken
places.blurb: A Jamaican takeout counter on Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn's Little Caribbean, run by Gavin Hussey, whose jerk chicken is dry-rubbed, washed with vinegar and charred black before it is hacked apart to order.

places.hours_text: Wednesday, Thursday and Sunday 11am–10pm; Friday and Saturday 11am–12:30am. Monday and Tuesday not posted.
places.name: Wingnutz
places.blurb: A sports bar on Millersport Highway in Williamsville, run by Ed and Alicia Wrazen, whose wings ran for thirteen years out of a Knights of Columbus hall before they had a restaurant.

places.name: Chickie's & Pete's
places.blurb: A Philadelphia sports bar and crab house that began as a Mayfair taproom in 1977 and now runs stadium, casino and airport rooms.

places.name: Bolton's Spicy Chicken & Fish
places.blurb: A small East Nashville counter at 624 Main Street selling spicy fried chicken and spicy fried fish, opened in 1997 by Bolton Matthews and Dolly Ingram. The recipe came down from Matthews's uncle Bolton Polk.

places.name: Central BBQ
places.blurb: A Memphis barbecue house started in 2002 by two competition cooks, Craig Blondis and Roger Sapp, on Central Avenue.

places.hours_text: Wednesday to Saturday 11 a.m. to 7 p.m.; Sunday noon to 6 p.m.; closed Monday and Tuesday
places.name: Ching's Hot Wings
places.blurb: A Memphis wing shop on Getwell Road, trading since 2003, selling whole wings by the piece from three to four hundred.

places.hours_text: Daily from 11 a.m. — the Midtown room
places.name: Hattie B's Hot Chicken
places.blurb: A Nashville hot chicken house founded by a father and son both named Nick Bishop, open in Midtown since 2012 and now in seven cities.

places.hours_text: Monday to Saturday 11 a.m. to 10 p.m.; Sunday closed — the Nolensville Pike shop
places.name: Prince's Hot Chicken Shack
places.blurb: The Nashville hot chicken shack, started by James Thornton Prince and run since 1980 by his great-niece André Prince Jeffries.

places.name: Bonchon
places.blurb: A Korean fried chicken chain that fries each piece twice and paints the sauce on with a brush.

places.name: Wingstop
places.blurb: A fast-food chain built on one part of the bird. Antonio Swad and Bernadette Fiaschetti opened the first Wingstop in Garland, Texas in 1994 and franchised it from 1997; the company is headquartered in Dallas and counted…
